Runs as a single thread block.\n// Records the smallest failing diagonal index in failIdx.\n__global__ void potrfDiagKernel(double* A, int n, int k0, int nb, int* failIdx) {\n    __shared__ double T[TILE][TILE + 1];\n    __shared__ bool failed;\n\n    const int t = threadIdx.x;\n    if (t == 0) failed = false;\n    if (t < nb) {\n        for (int c = 0; c < nb; ++c) {\n            T[t][c] = A[(size_t)(k0 + t) * n + k0 + c];\n        }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int j = 0; j < nb; ++j) {\n        // Diagonal element\n        if (t == 0) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += T[j][k] * T[j][k];\n            }\n            const double val = T[j][j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite\n                atomicMin(failIdx, k0 + j);\n                failed = true;\n            } else {\n                T[j][j] = sqrt(val);\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n        if (failed) break;\n\n        // Off-diagonal elements in column j\n        const int i = j + 1 + t;\n        if (i < nb) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += T[i][k] * T[j][k];\n            }\n            T[i][j] = (T[i][j] - sum) / T[j][j];\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (t < nb) {\n        for (int c = 0; c <= t; ++c) {\n            A[(size_t)(k0 + t) * n + k0 + c] = T[t][c];\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Solve L(i,K) * L(K,K)^T = A(i,K) for every row i below the diagonal tile.\n// Each thread handles one row; the diagonal tile is staged in shared memory.\n__global__ void trsmPanelKernel(double* A, int n, int k0, int nb) {\n    __shared__ double D[TILE][TILE + 1];\n\n    const int t = threadIdx.x;\n    for (int idx = t; idx < nb * nb; idx += blockDim.x) {\n        const int r = idx / nb;\n        const int c = idx % nb;\n        D[r][c] = A[(size_t)(k0 + r) * n + k0 + c];\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    const int i = k0 + nb + blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + t;\n    if (i >= n) return;\n\n    double* row = A + (size_t)i * n + k0;\n    for (int j = 0; j < nb; ++j) {\n        double sum = 0.0;\n        for (int k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n            sum += row[k] * D[j][k];\n        }\n        row[j] = (row[j] - sum) / D[j][j];\n    }\n}\n\n// Trailing update: A(r,c) -= sum_{k in panel} L(r,k) * L(c,k) for the lower-triangular\n// tiles (bi >= bj) of the trailing submatrix starting at t0. A[(size_t)gi * n + k0 + tx] : 0.0;\n        Rb[r][tx] = (gj < n && tx < nb) ? A[(size_t)gj * n + k0 + tx] : 0.0;\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int r = ty; r < TILE; r += blockDim.y) {\n        const int gr = t0 + bi * TILE + r;\n        const int gc = t0 + bj * TILE + tx;\n        if (gr < n && gc < n && gr >= gc) {\n            double acc = 0.0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < nb; ++k) {\n                acc += Ra[r][k] * Rb[tx][k];\n            }\n            A[(size_t)gr * n + gc] -= acc;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// C = X * X^T (+ diagAdd on the diagonal). Each dot product is accumulated in increasing k\n// order, the same order as the sequential reference loops.\n__global__ void gramKernel(const double* X, double* C, int n, double diagAdd) {\n    __shared__ double Xa[TILE][TILE + 1];\n    __shared__ double Xb[TILE][TILE + 1];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int i0 = blockIdx.y * TILE;\n    const int j0 = blockIdx.x * TILE;\n\n    double acc = 0.0;\n    for (int kc = 0; kc < n; kc += TILE) {\n        const int k = kc + tx;\n        const int gi = i0 + ty;\n        const int gj = j0 + ty;\n        Xa[ty][tx] = (gi < n && k < n) ? X[(size_t)gi * n + k] : 0.0;\n        Xb[ty][tx] = (gj < n && k < n) ? X[(size_t)gj * n + k] : 0.0;\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        const int kmax = min(TILE, n - kc);\n        for (int kk = 0; kk < kmax; ++kk) {\n            acc += Xa[ty][kk] * Xb[tx][kk];\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    const int i = i0 + ty;\n    const int j = j0 + tx;\n    if (i < n && j < n) {\n        C[(size_t)i * n + j] = (i == j) ? acc + diagAdd : acc;\n    }\n}\n\n// Per-row maxima of |R - A| and |R - A| / (|A| + 1e-10). One block per row.\n__global__ void errorKernel(const double* R, const double* A, int n, double* rowAbs, double* rowRel) {\n    __shared__ double sAbs[256];\n    __shared__ double sRel[256];\n\n    const int tid = threadIdx.x;\n    const int i = blockIdx.x;\n\n    double mAbs = 0.0;\n    double mRel = 0.0;\n    for (int j = tid; j < n; j += blockDim.x) {\n        const size_t idx = (size_t)i * n + j;\n        const double error = fabs(R[idx] - A[idx]);\n        mAbs = fmax(mAbs, error);\n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A[idx]) + 1e-10);\n        mRel = fmax(mRel, rel);\n    }\n    sAbs[tid] = mAbs;\n    sRel[tid] = mRel;\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int s = blockDim.x / 2; s > 0; s >>= 1) {\n        if (tid < s) {\n            sAbs[tid] = fmax(sAbs[tid], sAbs[tid + s]);\n int i = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;\n    if (i < n && j < n && j > i) {\n        A[(size_t)i * n + j] = 0.0;\n    }\n}\n\n// Device-side C = X * X^T (+ diagAdd on the diagonal)\nvoid gramDevice(const double* dX, double* dC, int n, double diagAdd) {\n    if (n == 0) return;\n    const int T = (n + TILE - 1) / TILE;\n    gramKernel<<<dim3(T, T), dim3(TILE, TILE)>>>(dX, dC, n, diagAdd);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    if (n == 0) return;\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B (sequential, so the sequence is reproducible)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    // Compute A = B * B^T on the GPU, adding n to the diagonal for diagonal dominance\n    double* dB = nullptr;\n    double* dA = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dB, n * n * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dA, n * n * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dB, B.data(), n * n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    gramDevice(dB, dA, static_cast<int>(n), static_cast<double>(n));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(A.data(), dA, n * n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dB));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dA));\n}\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    if (n == 0) return true;\n\n    const int N = static_cast<int>(n);\n    double* dA = nullptr;\n    int* dFail = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dA, n * n * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dFail, sizeof(int)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dA, A.data(), n * n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    const int noFailure = INT_MAX;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dFail, &noFailure, sizeof(int), i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfzaa3NyKD9uoRUiz9qWR","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Cholesky benchmark now runs its decomposition on the GPU, and the program always uses CUDA. The executable is still `cholesky`, and only `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt` changed. It builds cleanly with no warnings, and it passes validation at every size I tried (1, 2, 31, 32, 33, 100, 512, 1000, 2049).\n\n**Performance** (RTX 3090, timed region = decomposition including host↔device copies):\n\n| n | Original (CPU) | New (GPU) |\n|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 29 ms | 4 ms |\n| 2048 | 2139 ms | 22 ms |\n| 4096 | not measured | 79 ms (~290 GFLOPS) |\n\nThe 4096 figure is about half of the card's FP64 peak, so there is room to tune. I did not pursue that further.\n\n**What changed**\n- **Decomposition:** a blocked, right-looking Cholesky with 32-wide tiles. Each block column goes through three kernels: factor the diagonal tile, solve the panel below it, and update the trailing lower tiles. The upper triangle is zeroed on the device, as the original does.\n- **Failure path:** the reported index is the smallest failing diagonal element, as in the original. I checked this with a temporary copy outside the project that injects a bad diagonal at index 40. It reports 40 and exits with code 1.\n- **Matrix generation and `-v` validation:** these are also on the GPU. Neither is timed. Both keep the original per-element summation order.\n- **No new dependencies:** I wrote the kernels directly rather than using cuBLAS or cuSOLVER.\n- **CMake:** the project now enables the CUDA language and sets `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native`. The minimum CMake version is 3.24. `cholesky.cpp` is compiled as CUDA through a source-file property, so no new `.cu` file was needed. The host flags (`-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra`) are forwarded to the host compiler under nvcc.\n\n**Choices and caveats**\n- **Rounding differs slightly.** Blocking reorders the floating-point sums. With `-r`, the sample values agree with the original to about 1e-16 relative, but the `Hash:` line will not match the original's. If an external checker compares hashes exactly, it will fail.\n- **Timing scope.** The timer covers the host-to-device copy, the kernels, and the copy back. CUDA context setup is done before the timer starts, so it is not counted.\n- **Sanitizer not run.** `compute-sanitizer` is installed but its injection library is missing, so the boundary checks rely on the passing runs at non-multiple-of-32 sizes.\n- **Build location.** I built in `/tmp` so no build artifacts ended up in the project. `output.txt` was not modified by me."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":973,"cache_read_input_tokens":60334,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":973},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"944798ba-a34e-48db-9353-e2a137cf6074","uuid":"570e7301-7f0d-40ec-b270-88d3a67bbe38","timestamp":"2026-10-13T16:49:38.000Z","request_id":"req_011Cfzaa348sS4g8WecVY8cU"}
